native_name: Renault SA (Regie Nationale des Usines Renault until 1990)

selection.reason: The major French civilian manufacturer, with a sourced cross-country link to Japan through the Renault-Nissan alliance. It gives the pilot a civilian industrial identity and an alliance case that must not be confused with a merger.

existing_game_references.note: Generated fictional manufacturing contractors only; no real identity or car product consumer exists.

summary: The Regie Renault became a state-owned societe anonyme in 1990 and its privatisation became effective from 1996. Renault took 51% of Dacia in 1999 and 36.8% of Nissan in the 1999 alliance; Mitsubishi joined the alliance in 2016. Renault sold Nissan shares in 2023-2024, and from 30 June 2025 it no longer equity-accounts Nissan. Products in the window include the Clio (1990), Twingo (1992), ZOE (2012) and Renault 5 E-Tech (2024).

roles.role: vehicle manufacturer and group parent company

entities.note: The 1990 source records the change to a societe anonyme without spelling the new corporate name; later filings use Renault SA.

proposed.uncertainty: Cars have no product consumer: the supplier flow covers military designer platforms only. Manufacturing contractors improve funded industrial work; a real identity would replace one generated contractor, not add a firm with sales.

duplicates_avoided: Renault SA is not proposed for France:ground_apc; no Renault military product was researched and the VAB carrier line is not attributed to Renault SA.
Nissan, Dacia and Mitsubishi Motors are counterparties with their own identities, never Renault names.

integration_flow.summary: A later, reviewed integration could attach this sourced identity to a company created through the existing orders. Design stays with the commissioning country; Defense R&D pays development as work is performed; the company funds tooling, national-warehouse inputs and fabrication from its own settled cash; the buyer purchases whole finished units from company stock; delivery follows fiscal settlement and seven accessible days. No existing company order produces civilian cars; a Renault identity would first appear only as a sector contractor serving funded work.

steps.note: Paid capitalisation from Defense procurement (political capital price applies); leases one existing completed Arms Plant slot. No historical factory, balance or stock is granted.
Further paid working capital; unsettled receivables are not spendable cash.
Frozen design revision; Defense R&D pays engineering, prototype and trials work day by day; prototypes are never saleable.
Finite company-owned stock target (0-12 units); a target is never a government order.
Government buys whole units from existing company stock; settlement then seven accessible delivery days.

unmapped: Passenger cars and electric vehicles: no civilian product consumer.
Alliance cross-shareholding: no company-to-company ownership model exists.

gaps: The exact 1990 corporate name and effective date of the status change were not retrieved.
The Busan plant entry on the history page describes Samsung Motors in 1995 without dating Renault ownership; it is not used.

future_policy.note: Nothing after the frozen cutoff is predicted. Any later product, successor or business in a campaign must be authored as explicitly fictional game content (labelled "(fictional)") or left unknown.
